analysis.d_full: AENEAS, BY THE OPERATOR'S ADDRESS 'AENEAS DEEPMIND', ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'an artificial intelligence model developed by Google DeepMind (introduced in July 2025) designed to contextualize, restore, date, and locate ancient, damaged, or fragmentary Latin inscriptions.' The Latin Epigraphic Dataset ('over 176,000 inscriptions'), the multimodal input, gap restoration, dating 'within roughly 13 years', the historians' trial (90%, 44%), the Predicting the Past interface. Seven cards: DeepMind, the Google blog, Oxford's Faculty of Classics, GitHub, Nature, Predicting the Past, MIT Technology Review.
findings: THE MODEL HELD. Latin inscriptions, July 2025, and contextualizing by parallels ('to identify geographical provenance and shared syntax or formulas', 'useful contextual parallels 90% of the time') are the record's: 'the first artificial intelligence (AI) model for contextualizing ancient inscriptions', reasoning 'across thousands of Latin inscriptions, retrieving textual and contextual parallels in seconds'. Checked 2026-10-31 against the Revelation First census record of 2026-10-30 and the sources it saved.
THE REACH ABSENT. The blog: 'Our model can also be adapted to other ancient languages, scripts and media, from papyri to coinage'. The composition keeps the model to Latin stone.

THE PARTNERS. The body names Google DeepMind alone. The blog: 'We co-developed Aeneas with the University of Nottingham, and in partnership with researchers at the Universities of Warwick, Oxford and Athens University of Economics and Business'. The Predicting the Past card gives 'DeepMind, Durham University, Oxford, and partners'; Durham is not in the saved sources.

FIGURES FROM THE POST AND THE CARDS. The DeepMind post the census saved gives 'over 176,000 Latin inscriptions' and dating 'within 13 years'; the date span and the 44% come from the cards. The census row's 'thousands' was its own misreading, repaired 2026-10-31.

A QUALIFICATION DROPPED. 'Aeneas provided useful contextual parallels 90% of the time'. The paper (card 5): historians reported that the parallels 'could serve as a starting point for historical inquiry 75% of the time. This increased to 90% when Aeneas’ predictions' were added. The composition gives the combined figure to the parallels alone.
